candidates: In tutorial and example scripts under `examples/`, use `snake_case` for all variable names (e.g. `n2_distance`, not `N2_distance` or `N2Distance`). Flag any camelCase or PascalCase identifiers for correction.

Proofread narrative `# %%` comments in tutorial scripts for grammar and phrasing (e.g. missing articles, awkward constructions) before approving; these comments render as prose in the sphinx-gallery HTML output.

When a tutorial or example introduces a new Sphinx extension dependency (e.g. `sphinxcontrib-video`), make sure it is added to the `[docs]` optional-dependencies section in `pyproject.toml` in addition to any explicit `pip install` lines in `.gitlab-ci.yml`.

When a tutorial uses sphinx-gallery's `matplotlib_animations` feature to render mp4 animations, verify that `ffmpeg` is available in the CI doc-build environment (e.g. installed in the `ase-full-monty` Docker image or the `doc:` job's `before_script`); without it the build will fail with 'unknown file extension: .mp4'.
In `plt.subplots()` calls, prefer the explicit keyword-argument form (`nrows=2`) over bare positional arguments for clarity.
Tutorial examples added to the sphinx gallery should produce at least one piece of visual output (a static plot or an animation) so that the gallery page has a meaningful thumbnail.
